title: Dual whispering-gallery-mode emission from a naphthalimide-based microcavity for readable microbarcoding
content: Naphthalimide is an important fluorophore that has been extensively studied in organic chemistry owing to its excellent photophysical properties. However, its photonic behavior in polymer microcavities remains largely unexplored. The 4-pentyl-N-pentyl-1,8-naphthalimide (PNI) fluorophore exhibits distinct dual emission in a polystyrene matrix, and has been integrated into an optical microcavity to achieve excitation-switchable dual whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) emission. The fluorescence emission of PNI enables selective activation of two spectrally separated WGM outputs simply by varying the excitation wavelength. Exploiting this color-adaptable photonic response, we demonstrate a dual-mode microbarcoding platform capable of encoding multiple optical signatures within a single microscale resonator. This strategy establishes a simple molecular-to-photonic route towards compact, excitation-switchable microtagging systems for advanced security and anti-counterfeiting applications.
